headline: High: Prefect’s broad egress can exfiltrate workflow metadata while godot_rl_agents provides no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, Prefect can call external APIs and godot_rl_agents has no io_surfaces or sandboxing fields, so if operators bridge them via files or copied outputs, injected instructions could propagate. The pathway is inferred, not proven.
conditions: IF an operator copies Prefect output into godot_rl_agents prompts or files
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste of untrusted Prefect output into agent prompts
Add a manual review step before any handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad network egress, while godot_rl_agents has no documented data-class handling or isolation. If they share a workspace or Prefect receives files from the game agent, metadata or embedded content can flow outward by default. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file tree
IF Prefect is configured to ingest artifacts produced by godot_rl_agents
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Restrict Prefect runs to metadata-only inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent ACLs on shared storage

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no write or network surfaces, while Prefect exposes API calls and broad egress. That means overlapping mutable-resource writes are not documented, so a true capability conflict is unlikely. Uncertainty is limited because the profiles do not show shared write targets or locking issues.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or repo
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state without locking
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents write access to the same path
Add explicit locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestrator, so it may treat upstream outputs as actionable workflow metadata, while godot_rl_agents can emit simulation results that could be forwarded without verification. The profiles do not prove this handoff, but the default orchestration pattern makes a verification gap plausible and potentially impactful.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes godot_rl_agents outputs as authoritative workflow inputs
IF no validation step is inserted before downstream actions
mitigations: Add schema validation on all handoffs
Require human approval for downstream actions
Log and diff upstream outputs before use

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Prefect handles workflow metadata and godot_rl_agents has no touched data classes, so compliance risk is limited to future deployments that introduce regulated data. The other agent is not cited because no specific compliance surface is shown for it beyond open-source docs.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Prefect workflows
IF retention or residency policies differ across deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
